Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PoroTomo DAS, Brady Hot Springs, March 2016):

RECORDS & ANOMALIES
- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20; 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping context: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, LBNL/NCEDC magnitudes, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5) — this is the calibrated probability:
  b      Sigma      P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) over observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449     0.0001198      5.236e-06                        0.03719
  0.73   -5.319     0.004922       0.0002155                        0.2809
  0.65   -5.281     0.01474        0.0006484                        0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at/above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts) — this is the upper bound, not calibrated:
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based estimate gives P(Mw>=5.5) of roughly 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year across b = 1.0 to 0.65 (a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is unlikely over this ~16-day window, ~5e-6 to ~6.5e-4 in the observed volume), while the DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr is much higher because uncalibrated DAS magnitudes over-count events, so it should be treated only as an upper bound.
